title: Cipher sheets and keys in the Elizabethan and early Stuart State Papers Foreign
shelfmark: TNA SP 98/1/22 (1588 'Cipher from AB'); SP 85/2/99 (c. 1601 'Mr Wilson's cipher for his man'); SP 78/87/152 (1630 note with cipher symbols); SP 78/101/64 (1636 De Vic, sheet of cipher); SP 78/102/75 (1636 Scudamore, sheet of cipher); SP 81/39/402 (c. 1632, two sheets of cipher fragments)
note: Bare keys, no ciphertext on the item. Useful against SP 78 and SP 81 despatches of the same envoys; not checked whether the matching letters are deciphered.

title: Key to the cypher used by Sir Edward Wood, English envoy to Sweden, 1672
note: Key only; the Swedish despatches SP 95 of 1672 are the ciphertext family.

title: Cipher for names of towns in France (18th century); key to a cipher among the Molinos and Innocent XII papers (PRO 30/50/8)
note: Two undated key records in private papers; no matching ciphertext identified.

title: Edward Murphy's cypher sent to Pitt, 1757, with an 'Account of a New Invention'
note: An invention and its key, not an operational cipher.

title: Seized cipher papers and 'Cypher found among Dr Jernegan's papers' (SP 35/40 part 2, 1665-1723 file); Layer's cipher-key BY1 (SP 35/39/21, 1722)
note: Atterbury-plot era keys, see catalogue 860 and the SP 35 key volumes; SP 35/39/21 BY1 is the key for the Layer papers.

title: Prospectus for a cypher system (17th century)
note: A proposal, not an operational key.

title: Stepney's cipher with glossed words and Wallis's decipherments, Vienna/Berlin 1693-94
shelfmark: TNA SP 105/84/113 (four words in cipher glossed 'Minister S'); SP 105/60/82 (Wallis's decipherments of intercepts)
note: Partial decipher glosses; SP 105/60/121 is already a lead.

title: List of code names in the intercepted Cameron of Gleneves letter, 1751
note: Partial key by the intercepting side; the ciphertext is the candidates.json row for SP 54/41/27.

title: Kitchener papers, Nile expedition telegrams 1884-85 'in code', 'code and translation', 'partial decode'
note: Already lead 1159 in leads.json; about 15 items carry a translation or decode, so they are key pairs for the Wolseley/Wilson telegram code (not a new row).
